title: Glasgow Hotel Deals: City Centre, West End & Riverside
description: Compare Glasgow hotel prices on every big booking site. Stay in the Merchant City, the West End or by the river near the big concert venues and SEC.
intro: Live music, galleries and grand Victorian streets: compare Glasgow hotel prices for your dates on every site.

sections.html: The SEC and the OVO Hydro by the River Clyde host big concerts and conferences, and hotels nearby fill fast on event nights. Compare early, or stay in the centre and take a short train or taxi.

sections.h2: Which part of Glasgow should you stay in?
sections.html: The city centre, around Glasgow Central and Queen Street stations, is the easiest base if you are arriving by train or want shops and restaurants on your doorstep. The Merchant City, just east of the centre, is known for its bars and restaurants. The West End, around Byres Road and Kelvingrove Park, is quieter and suits visitors heading to the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum or the University of Glasgow. Staying near the River Clyde puts you close to the SEC and OVO Hydro venues. Whichever you choose, use the compare form above to check the same dates on several booking sites, and look at the exact distance from the hotel to the station or venue on the booking page.

sections.h2: Tips for booking a Glasgow hotel
sections.html:
• Check for events. Concerts and conferences at the big venues can affect availability, so compare early on event dates.
  • Read the cancellation terms. Our guide to free cancellation and your UK booking rights explains what to look for.
  • Look at the total price. See our guide to hidden hotel fees and fake discounts.
  • Combine with Edinburgh. Compare Edinburgh hotels if you are planning a two-city Scotland trip.

faqs.q: Is Glasgow good value for a city break?
faqs.a: Glasgow often has a wide choice of hotels across the centre, the West End and the riverside, so comparing sites can turn up good value, especially away from big event nights.

faqs.q: Which area of Glasgow is best for a first visit?
faqs.a: The city centre near Glasgow Central and Queen Street stations is the most convenient for most first-time visitors, with the Merchant City and West End as popular alternatives depending on whether you want nightlife or a quieter base.

faqs.q: How do I compare Glasgow hotel prices?
faqs.a: Use the compare form to open the same dates on several booking sites, then check the total price including any fees and the cancellation terms before you choose.
